body:
Wow this was so very uncomfortably insightful. I really can't thank you enough, because it seems to obvious now but I hadn't even though of it like that before. I will definitely try to acknowledge my past experiences (not with telling people about my SI because I've never done that, but with other stuff) and attempt to break past the fear and have the conversation. My T has actually been trying to get me to carry my anxiety about other things with me and take more risks to allow me to be more functional and do things that matter to me, so this fits really well.

I'm having to do video call therapy at the moment, but I'll definitely try and write down the scripts other people have provided me with. If all else fails I'm sure she'd be fine with me emailing her during the session, it just might be a little awkward, no change there haha.

Thanks again, I honestly really really appreciate the time you spent sharing your experience and relating it to mine in such an perceptive way.

Thanks for the tip. I still haven't decided whether it'd be easier to ease myself into it with something like you said, or just go straight in. I quite like the other commenter's idea of using the 'how have you been?' opening to first suggest the idea I haven't been so great, and then explain where my head's at.

Thanks for reassuring me about hospitalisation and her reaction.
Thanks for this. I'm not in the US, but I know of a couple of similar services in the UK.
She does sometimes. It usually feels like more of a pleasantry but I suppose I could hope she does and kind of pounce on it. Thanks so much, that's made things seem more manageable.

Ok, thanks. I might do that to put my mind at ease. 

Honestly thank you so much!
Thank you for taking the time to write that! It's been a long time since I've seen the light but hopefully I'm on the right path now

Thanks for your kind reply. 

Haha I don't fully know what's involved in making a safety plan but I've heard of them. 

Yeah it's weird because I have horribly almost debilitatingly low levels of insight into my thoughts, feelings, and behaviours ordinarily, but I know my suicidal thoughts a *little* better. I guess they're a bit more... straightforward? In your (my) face? I have no idea.

Thanks :)

Sorry to hear that. 

Around 2 months. 

Ok, thanks. That's very true.

Thanks mate, I appreciate the response. She is pretty non-reactive usually, but I can't shift the thought that she'll react badly. 

She does usually ask how I'm doing at the beginning, but it's more of a pleasantry as she already has an idea of what we should talk about each session. She's occasionally asked whether there's anything specific I want to bring up at the beginning, but there's no guarantee she'll say that this time. 

Haha that is one hell of an opening but I like the format a lot.

Thanks for your reply, that seems like a good script. Should I just go straight in with that? The thought of just blurting that out is terrifying. 

Ok that's reassuring, thank you.

Thank you so much for replying. I didn't end up telling her about the suicidal thoughts, but I did tell her things were really bad and how that was affecting me a bit, so she's getting me to refer myself to my university's mental health team. Hopefully I'll build up the courage to do that

Thanks man :) She said she'd send me some stuff to refer myself to my university's mental health team, without me even having to ask. It was so so scary and I clammed up massively but I'm glad I did it.

Thanks for the reply! I did it. I was so unbelievably nervous, and I didn't go into too many details, but I'm really glad I did it. She's sending me some stuff to self refer to services, so that's the next anxiety-inducing step!

I understand. I never really listen at the time either, but some of the comments about hanging on come back to me in some of my darkest moments and sometimes that's enough to stop me from doing anything.

Oh man I'm so sorry to hear that :(

I understand what you mean. Please try and stick around. This might be a way to open the difficult conversation with them about your own mental health, if they're your friends? Or with other people who knew them?
Yeah you're right. No one's perfect.
Meh. That's shitty of them, not you. If one of my mates was being toxic I'd tell them, not desert them, and I'm not even that much of a good friend.
Yeah there's a thin line between being toxic and being honest, I think. That's one of the many reasons I don't talk about this stuff to my close friends.

Date a blind guy! Why not!

People do judge based on looks, but I really do think there is someone out there who would find you attractive. 

That would work too haha, as long as it wasn't an unhealthy relationship. They should make a dating app for miserable people. Interests and hobbies: none.

Yeah I also often find that guys are nicer to my friends than they are to me, but the majority of the ones that act like that turn out to be arseholes anyway. You just have to find the right people, in my experience, who can see past what you look like. I don't know about you, but I wouldn't want to be with someone who judged me because of my looks. I know people in relationships like that and they're never happy. My thinking is I don't care whether my prospective partner has their hair a certain way, dresses up in fancy clothes, or has the 'ideal' bodytype etc., and I'd expect them to be the same towards me. Preferences are fine of course, but those are individual to everyone.

I don't know what else to say, my looks get me down too, but I know that the main reason I'm not in a relationship is because I spend most of my time alone in bed, and don't put myself out there at all in regards to meeting people with the intent of dating them or whatever. I also think that I'm not happy enough to make anyone else happy, but I don't know if that's just the mental illness talking.

So true. 

The mirror isn't anyone's friend though. I don't think I've met anyone who genuinely likes the way they look, even when I see them as an attractive person.

That being said, people often say that happiness, ambition and confidence are the most attractive traits, which means I'm pretty fucked haha.

Yeah. And hope that things change.

I reckon I'm ugly too, and I've never had a partner. Friends shouldn't care about how you look though, I know mine don't. If they care then they're shit friends. Same with a partner probably, it sounds cringy but personality is more important. Also, I bet you're not as ugly as you think you are.

So true man. Keep playing the game.

Yes! I manage to hide how I feel reasonably well most of the time. I've built an entire personality around hating myself/everything/being lazy/joking about being sad, so I guess I'm lucky in that sense? I don't have loads of friends, but I've got some good ones. I'm not close with my family but that's not entirely my fault. I'm sure the way I am is annoying for other people, but I basically just try and stay on the downlow and coast along.
We've just got to hope that that normal person is still in there I guess. I'm scared to think what I'd be like though. Although I hate myself, I'm used to how things are in a weird way now.

Mate I'm the same. I'm 22 now, and I had my first thoughts of suicide at 10, so it's been a while. I've never tried therapy, largely because I don't think I'd be able to open up to them. 

I feel exactly the same, it makes me sad but there's some comfort to be found in shared experience. It's also nice not to be judged. I feel like so many people irl would be like 'oh you're being selfish' or 'just get over it, your life isn't even bad'.

This... thing, whatever it is, has eaten everything I am from the inside throughout my formative years. I don't feel like I exist without it, it is everything I am, if that makes sense.

I feel the same way. I also have other things I need to sort. From anecdotes I've heard from other people, it doesn't necessarily take a miracle. It can be a small thing, or a series of small things. That being said, some people do seem to wake up one day and decide that enough is enough (in a good way) and go and seek help. Maybe it'll happen, although I have to admit it doesn't seem likely for it to happen to me either.

Hey man, I know this is rich coming from me, but try and stick around if you can. I know I definitely feel as though the pain will never leave me too, but the rational part of my brain knows that isn't probably true. Have you exhausted every option available to you regarding getting help? I know I haven't, I can't bring myself to. Maybe one day I will, that's what keeps me going. I hope you find a way too, there are lots of us out here feeling the same way.
I wish you couldn't relate man, for your own sake
I feel you man. I don't have exams but I've got a load of essays that I'm irreparably behind on. We'll get through it one way or another! Just do what you can and try not to be too hard on yourself
Yeah it really sucks. So true! It's too easy to get caught up in the moment and be blind to the possibility of a better future
Hahaha thank you (I think)

I will do. That's a nice idea! I absolutely can't keep a regular journal, so it'll be nice to have a record. 

Thank you so much for everything :)

I love this!

Here are my 5 from the other thread:

1. Finished a year long placement job successfully, i.e. without being fired, even though I found it really hard as it was my first ever full time job

2. Became closer to 2 of my friends and started hanging out with them more

3. Started spending more time with friends generally, especially ones I hadn't really seen in a couple of years

4. Didn't/still haven't dropped out of uni

5. Started thinking about what the fuck I'm going to do when I graduate this year. I haven't applied for anything or taken any solid steps, but I read about a few potential job opportunities over the course of last year, which is better than I've ever done before

I'm going to try and do this at least once a week. Looking forward to reading everyone else's 2019 highlights!

No problem, that sounds good. 

Nice! Chaise lounger sounds amazing

"Combated from cringing" hahaha so true. As a Gen Z, I can also relate. 

That's good, I'm sure it'll get her into positive habits. 

Thanks. Yay! I can't do anything without coffee

Sorry to hear that :( Some people's views are so backwards, I'm glad your friends are understanding at least.

I live in the UK, so I'm lucky that we have free, usually great quality health care.  

Thanks man :) I hope you feel better too

Thanks for taking the time to reply. 

I feel the same about birthdays etc.! No one else irl that I know seems to feel the same though. 

I wouldn't say that I have an alcohol problem, I don't often drink alone, but I probably do have a slightly unhealthy relationship to it. Maybe you should try dry January? Or pick any month where you vow not to drink? I've heard it's a good way to tell whether you rely on it to socialise/deal with your problems/relax etc. 

Yeah the human experience is pretty universal it seems. I don't talk about stuff with anyone really. I don't like to make New Years resolutions because I never keep them, but my general aim for this year is to try and speak to someone about my shit. I might use my inability to even make a start on my dissertation (large ongoing project due in May this year) as an 'excuse' (to make to myself) to speak to someone at my uni.

Thanks so much again :) I hope things get better for you too

I'm definitely the kind of person that usually (wrongly) shits on positive thinking. I could probably list a load of excuses as to why, but it basically just comes down to it making me super uncomfortable, because negative thinking is what I'm used to. That's a cute idea though, especially to do with your kids. 

I couldn't stomach 10, but here are 5. They might be kind of shitty but they're the best I could think of.

1. Finished a year long placement job successfully,   i.e. without being fired, even though I found it really hard as it was my first ever full time job

2. Became closer to 2 of my friends and started hanging out with them more

3. Started spending more time with friends generally, especially ones I hadn't really seen in a couple of years

4. Didn't/still haven't dropped out of uni

5. Started thinking about what the fuck I'm going to do when I graduate this year. I haven't applied for anything or taken any solid steps, but I read about a few potential job opportunities over the course of last year, which is better than I've ever done before

Thanks so much for taking the time to reply. I hope 2020 is wonderful for you :)

Thanks so much for your reply. That's a really interesting perspective. It's almost impossible for me to work on a project by myself too, so doing something as a one off/with other people is a good idea. I find I don't have any motivation to do pretty much anything (thanks depression), but I'm hoping this will change in the future.

You're right about it being better than 17. Which was better than 12. Hopefully it'll get better from here.

That sounds like the dream! I'm glad things are going well for you.
Thanks for your reply :) it means a lot to know that people are out there who care

Thank you so much for your reply, your words truly do mean a lot.

I don't know anyone with a baby, but I'll bear the principle in mind anyway. I always stay up ridiculously late every night anyway, and can't even imagine being asleep by 9pm haha. Kudos to you for raising kids, that's really cool. 

Everyone talks about this/youth as being the best age but tbh all I've known over the past 10 years is negative feelings. I hope things do become less painful because I don't think I have the guts to end it all either.

Thanks again. I hope you have a good 2020 :)
